task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Is the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes, initiations or same-position minutes) the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types?
How can primary types, gainers and profile similarity be defined without outcome-derived labels or look-ahead?
Does any selector beat the base rate implied by roster size, and by the simple 'most initiations' or 'most minutes' baselines?
How many independent spells and cases are available once overlapping absences are clustered by team-season and absent player?
How should regression to the mean, measure reliability and confounding from lineup changes be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Exploratory map of about 23 absences. Mean replacement similarity was +0.863 for ABSORBED versus +0.848 for CASCADE. Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19, wrong-signed. Embiid 2023-24 cascaded with Reed at similarity 0.94. Recorded verdict: null; failure type B_powered_null; sample and power NOT_RECORDED; labelled non-confirmatory; automated adjudication, not human. Recorded failure evidence: similarity does not separate absorption from cascade and is almost always findable.

Connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (n=96 matched pairs versus role occupants; n=25 versus terminal). Related to the Player_absence_spells dataset. [prior work] lists the risks MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. It does not test which teammate gains.

Portability study: a mover's displacement signature is more similar across franchises than profile-matched decoys' signatures (median Delta +0.0557, perm p=0.005). It shows profile-matched decoys can be a useful comparison device. It does not address within-team gainers.
Feasibility gate passed (about 294 movers; displacement signature not collinear with play-type profile). The mover count and rho changed between the preregistration record and the final output.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using replacement-profile similarity to separate absorption from cascade, with mean similarity by outcome and a Spearman correlation on about 23 absences.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null. Similarity was wrong-signed and almost always findable. [prior work] also carries LABEL_ERROR / label_or_classification_error as a limitation. Sample and power are NOT_RECORDED, so how well powered the null was is not verifiable from [prior work].

evidence_establishes: One exploratory, non-confirmatory record ([prior work][prior work], inconclusive, verdict null) found no positive relation between similar-profile availability and absorption versus cascade; the correlation was wrong-signed.
Absence spells and play-type initiation records exist as datasets and have been used before ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
Profile-matched decoys and permutation or sign tests have been used successfully in this project (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: That the closest-profile teammate is not the largest gainer. [prior work][prior work] tested a different outcome (absorb versus cascade, not the identity of the top gainer), on about 23 absences, with unrecorded power and no validation.
Whether most minutes, most initiations or same-position minutes predict the top gainer.
Any hit rate against a chance or roster-size baseline.
Anything about the 148 spells or 11 cases now available.
own_inferences: Because 'closest profile' is nearly always findable and similarity was uninformative in the prior exploratory work, the profile-similarity selector is likely to perform near chance. The usage and minutes selectors may hit more often, but mainly because high-usage teammates have more room to gain in absolute terms.
The question has four selectors with a loosely defined 'largest gainer', so it needs one pre-specified primary selector. Without that, it invites multiple testing.

Selectors are correlated: the closest-profile teammate is often a high-minute, high-initiation teammate. The tests are therefore not independent, and the contrast that matters is similarity beyond a minutes or initiations baseline.

The unit counts are inconsistent (148 units, 148 spells, 11 cases). The independent-case count may be as low as 11, which would give little power to distinguish a hit rate of about 0.35 from about 0.25.
Absolute gains favor high-volume teammates mechanically. Gains in rate or share, and the effect of regression to the mean, need separate handling.
uncertainties: The meaning of the '11 cases' and how it relates to the 148 spells is not stated.
How the absent player's primary types are defined, whether from pre-absence data only, and how many types per player.
The minimum minutes or possessions required for a teammate to count as a candidate, and the typical number of candidates per spell.
Absence spell definition (DNP, injury, rest, ejection) and whether absences are exogenous.
Whether the 2025-26 data are complete, and how the derived play-type possession labels were validated.
The power and sample details of [prior work][prior work] are NOT_RECORDED.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I might have proceeded to a simple hit-rate test. [prior work][prior work] (inconclusive, null, wrong-signed, non-confirmatory) lowers the expected support for the similarity hypothesis and shows that similarity is almost always findable. It pushes the design toward baseline-controlled, multiplicity-limited tests, and toward only a minimal confirmatory attempt. It does not settle the question, because it tested a different outcome on about 23 absences.

blocking_constraints.text: The ambiguous unit counts (148 spells, but only 11 cases) leave perhaps 11 independent cases. That is probably too few for a hit-rate test of four selectors against a roster-size baseline.
Four selectors (similarity, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) with an undefined primary one inflate the false-positive risk unless one is pre-specified.
'Primary types' and 'largest gainer' must come from pre-absence data only. Defining primary types from absence-period usage would make the test circular.

prior_work.summary: One exploratory, non-confirmatory record found similarity to be uninformative for absorb versus cascade (null, inconclusive). No record tests the identity of the largest gainer or the minutes, initiations and same-position selectors. The question is therefore only partly addressed, and only indirectly.

risks.text: Few independent cases. Spells for the same player or team-season are correlated, so the effective sample is small.
With about 8-10 candidates per spell and a few dominant ones, chance and 'top-usage teammate' hit rates are high. Raw hit rates would mislead without baselines.
Four selectors times several types times several definitions of gain.
Starters, injuries to other players, opponent, schedule, trades and coach changes alter the reorganization. Minutes and similarity are correlated.
Primary types or the profile definition could leak absence-period information.
The pre-absence window must end before the first absent game. Rolling profiles must not include the absence.
Teammates with a recent low initiation share may rebound mechanically. Absences are often selected on circumstance.
Initiation-type shares are noisy in small samples, and the profile similarity measure is noisy for low-volume players.
Derived play-type labels from play-by-play may be misclassified. [prior work][prior work] carries this limitation.
Absolute gains scale with baseline volume. Shares sum to a constant, so gains and losses are coupled ([prior work][prior work] lists this risk).

design.estimand: Primary: for each absence spell, the within-spell rank (or probability) of the teammate with the highest profile similarity to the absent player among candidates, on the gain in the absent player's pre-registered primary types, in excess of a baseline predictor (the teammate with the highest pre-absence initiation volume in those types). Secondary: the same for most minutes, most initiations and most same-position minutes. Gain = absence-period share of team initiations in those types minus the pre-absence share.
design.unit: Absence spell (absent player x team x contiguous missed games), clustered by absent player and team-season for inference. The first step is to reconcile 148 units, 148 spells and 11 cases and report the number of independent clusters.
design.sample: Spells in 2022-23 to 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs, 2025-26 as of the data freeze) in which the absent player has at least a pre-specified number of pre-absence initiations in primary types, the spell lasts at least a pre-specified minimum number of games, and at least 4 teammates exceed a minimum minutes/possession threshold. Primary types are the top 2 types by share of the absent player's initiations in a pre-absence window that ends before the spell. Exclude garbage time and spells where multiple rotation players are absent, or analyze those separately.
design.power: To be computed before looking at outcomes using the actual cluster count and candidate counts. Simulate the hit rate against a permutation baseline, with the smallest effect of interest set in advance (for example, a hit rate 15 points above the volume baseline). If fewer than about 30 independent clusters remain, label the analysis descriptive and exploratory, as in [prior work][prior work], and do not report a confirmatory decision.
design.controls: Compare against (a) a uniform random-candidate baseline, (b) a highest-usage/volume-in-type baseline, and (c) profile-matched decoy teammates, as in FAM:[prior work]. Use a logistic or conditional-logit model on candidates within spell with similarity, minutes, initiations and position-minutes as joint predictors, so that similarity is judged beyond volume. Adjust for starter status, other absences and trades. Use shares and rates, not just counts, and handle regression to the mean using candidate pre-absence baselines.
design.falsification: Placebo: apply the same procedure to matched pseudo-absences, games in which the absent player played, to estimate the hit rate expected from normal game-to-game variation. Reverse-sign check: the least similar teammate should not be the top gainer. Permutation of similarity within spell. The hypothesis is rejected for similarity if its incremental effect over the volume baseline has a confidence interval excluding the pre-specified minimum effect.
design.multiplicity: One primary confirmatory test (similarity beyond the volume baseline, primary types, share gain). The three other selectors are secondary and are adjusted by Holm correction or reported as exploratory. The definition of gain is frozen before analysis.
design.decision_rule: Support for similarity only if the cluster-robust incremental hit rate over the volume baseline exceeds the pre-specified margin, the permutation p is below 0.05 after correction, and the placebo is near baseline. A result consistent with the baseline counts as rejected only if the power analysis shows adequate power to detect the minimum effect. Otherwise label it inconclusive or exploratory. If the independent cluster count is too small (the 11-case reading), do not claim confirmation.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-11-01 (2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13, playoffs from 2026-06-21), with the derived play-type possession records from [source] database. Freeze the build and label-derivation version, and record the hash of the spell list before any outcome is examined.
